html:
The Cuica were a people of the Venezuelan Andes, in what is now Trujillo state. With the Timote to their south they are often grouped as the Timoto-Cuica peoples.

They farmed the mountain slopes with terraces and irrigation channels, growing maize, potatoes and other crops, and kept stores of food. Their villages were among the most settled farming communities of what is now Venezuela in the 1400s, though smaller than those of the Muisca to the southwest. The Spanish founded the city of Trujillo in their land in 1557, and conquest, forced labour and disease destroyed their society within a few generations. Their descendants merged into the rural mestizo population of the Andes.
